claims.text: The low-field magnetocaloric response of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films and nanoribbons is predominantly governed by local interfacial strain and defect-induced magnetic anisotropy.
Magnetic hysteresis in these films and nanoribbons is predominantly governed by local interfacial strain and defect-induced magnetic anisotropy.
Rapid low-dimensional deposition produces local stress fields and microstructural imperfections in FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons.
These stress fields and microstructural imperfections modulate magnetic phase transitions.
These stress fields and microstructural imperfections modulate heat-dissipation rates.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi nanoscale films and patterned nanoribbons have high internal strain and defect densities typical of rapid deposition.
A controlled post-deposition annealing treatment will be applied to partially relieve interfacial strain and reduce defect density.
Heat-transfer limitations are significant during magnetic-cooling cycles at approximately 1–5 Hz in the proposed nanoscale geometries.
Interfacial strain and defect density locally modify magnetic anisotropy.
Annealing relaxes residual stresses at interfaces.
Annealing reduces defect concentrations at interfaces.
Reduced residual stress and defect concentration moderate localized magnetic anisotropy.
Moderating localized magnetic anisotropy alters magnetic-field-induced phase transitions that contribute to the magnetocaloric effect.
Annealed samples will exhibit less magnetic hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will show a shifted magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing will produce a more reversible temperature change per magnetic-field cycle.
As-deposited films or ribbons have pronounced hysteresis.
The magnetocaloric behavior of the as-deposited films or ribbons differs from bulk responses.
